Requiring the use of a Just-in-Time (JIT) access model and conducting a full internal audit immediately afterward.
Formally documenting the risk acceptance of the elevated privileges and establishing an explicit time-of-day access restriction.
Implementing two-person control for the session and ensuring the administrator has signed a Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA).
Questions.AnswerKey: Formally documenting the risk acceptance of the elevated privileges and establishing an explicit time-of-day access restriction.
Questions.Explaination: Due Diligence requires that any acceptance of heightened risk (like granting an exception to Least Privilege) is formally documented and approved, including defined boundaries and expiration. Documenting the risk acceptance is paramount. Establishing explicit time-of-day restriction or short duration access (part of JIT, the close distractor) defines the boundary of the exception, minimizing the risk window. While compensating controls are necessary, formal risk acceptance provides the managerial accountability.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A CISO must validate the operational effectiveness of all security controls associated with a vendor handling customer data over the previous 12 months. The CISO also needs a report that focuses on security principles, not financial controls, to meet regulatory scrutiny. Which specific audit report should the CISO demand and why?
Choices: A SOC 1 Type I report, confirming control design suitability at a point in time.
A SOC 2 Type II report, confirming control effectiveness over a time period.
A SOC 1 Type II report, confirming financial control effectiveness over a time period.
An external penetration test report showing technical vulnerabilities.
Questions.AnswerKey: A SOC 2 Type II report, confirming control effectiveness over a time period.
Questions.Explaination: The request requires validation of security controls (SOC 2) and assurance of effectiveness over time (Type II). This combination provides the highest level of assurance regarding security operations effectiveness. The best distractor, SOC 1 Type II, is incorrect because SOC 1 focuses on controls relevant to financial reporting (secondary concern), not security and availability (SOC 2).

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A new manufacturing plant requires securing its physical perimeter. The CISO mandates the installation of perimeter fences, biometric access readers on all facility entrances, and the deployment of 24/7 security guards. Which control classification pair BEST describes the combined strategic functionality of these measures?
Choices: Fences/Biometrics (Preventive) and Guards (Corrective).
Fences (Deterrent) and Biometrics (Preventive).
Fences/Biometrics (Preventive) and Guards (Detective/Deterrent).
All elements function primarily as Detective controls in a layered approach.
Questions.AnswerKey: Fences/Biometrics (Preventive) and Guards (Detective/Deterrent).
Questions.Explaination: Fences and biometric readers are Preventive controls because they actively stop unauthorized access before it occurs. Security guards primarily act as Detective controls (spotting unauthorized activity during patrols) but also serve as Deterrent controls (discouraging attempts). The most accurate combination must reflect the highest level of control applied by the key elements, ruling out the singular classification of Deterrent only.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The security team suspects a memory-resident rootkit is active on a production server. The Incident Commander needs to ensure that the collection of volatile evidence is performed correctly while adhering to legal admissibility standards. Which sequence of actions is mandatory for the forensic investigator?
Choices: Initiate the Chain of Custody (COC), unplug the system, and then collect the RAM dump.
Document the scene, collect the RAM dump, and immediately generate a cryptographic hash of the memory image.
Collect the RAM dump, calculate the hash, and then initiate the COC documentation.
Unplug the system, check the system clock (NTP), and then document the physical scene.
Questions.AnswerKey: Document the scene, collect the RAM dump, and immediately generate a cryptographic hash of the memory image.
Questions.Explaination: The accepted forensic standard dictates collecting evidence in order of volatility. The required steps are: 1) Secure the scene and document/photograph it, 2) Collect the most volatile evidence (RAM/memory dump), and 3) Calculate the cryptographic hash of the acquired image to prove its integrity. Initiating the COC must happen before collection begins, but the physical action sequence is documentation followed by collection. Unplugging the system (the best distractor) would destroy the memory evidence.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A major utility provider is designing an emergency response plan for its SCADA systems. Due to the high risk to human safety, the CISO must ensure that all systems that fail (power loss, software crash) prioritize personnel escape and recovery actions. Which pair of security principles MUST be upheld in this design?
Choices: Fail Securely and Principle of Least Privilege.
Fail Open and Protection of Life Safety.
Defense in Depth and Separation of Duties.
Secure Defaults and Economy of Mechanism.
Questions.AnswerKey: Fail Open and Protection of Life Safety.
Questions.Explaination: The paramount priority in any security decision is Protection of Life Safety, which mandates that physical access mechanisms (especially egress points) must default to a state that allows unrestricted escape (Fail Open) during a failure. Fail Securely (the best distractor) is the opposite principle, prioritizing asset protection, which is subordinate to human life in an emergency.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A security analyst is analyzing the logs after a reported attack, attempting to piece together the attacker's timeline by correlating events across the firewall, web server, and database. The inability to establish a reliable chronological sequence indicates a failure to enforce which two core administrative controls?
Choices: Mandatory separation of duties and least privilege.
Network Time Protocol (NTP) synchronization and centralized logging (SIEM).
Cryptographic hashing of logs and WORM media storage.
Consistent log file naming conventions and annual audit reviews.
Questions.AnswerKey: Network Time Protocol (NTP) synchronization and centralized logging (SIEM).
Questions.Explaination: Inconsistent chronology (the core problem) is solved by enforcing NTP synchronization across all systems. To correlate events across multiple disparate sources (firewall, server, DB), logs must be collected and analyzed centrally, typically via a SIEM. Cryptographic hashing (the best distractor) is for integrity proof over time, not for initial chronological consistency.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The CISO requires a comprehensive strategy for validating the long-term effectiveness of security controls and identifying weaknesses resulting from configuration drift, rather than just known vulnerabilities. Which strategic process provides the best mechanism for meeting this ongoing assurance requirement?
Choices: Executing annual third-party penetration testing to identify exploitable flaws.
Implementing continuous security monitoring (CSM) using the NIST 800-137 framework.
Conducting annual security risk assessments (RA) to quantify residual risk.
Mandating quarterly vulnerability assessments (VA) against all production assets.
Questions.AnswerKey: Implementing continuous security monitoring (CSM) using the NIST 800-137 framework.
Questions.Explaination: Continuous Security Monitoring (CSM) is the strategic, ongoing process specifically designed to validate the continued operational effectiveness of security controls against established baselines and compliance requirements over time. Annual penetration testing and vulnerability assessments (the close distractors) are point-in-time assessments that capture the current state but fail to provide the continuous oversight required to detect subtle configuration drift or long-term control degradation.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A security manager is selecting a backup methodology for a high-volume data warehouse. The business mandates an RTO (time to restore service) of 6 hours, and an RPO (data loss tolerance) of 4 hours. Which backup type should the manager select to minimize the risk of missing the RTO, even if it sacrifices daily storage efficiency?
Choices: Incremental backup strategy due to its storage efficiency.
Differential backup strategy due to its simple two-file restoration process.
Transaction log backup strategy due to its ability to meet the RPO requirement.
Daily full backups using RAID 1 mirroring.
Questions.AnswerKey: Differential backup strategy due to its simple two-file restoration process.
Questions.Explaination: Meeting a tight RTO is challenged most by the complexity of file handling. Differential backups simplify the restoration process (requiring only the last full backup and the latest differential file), drastically reducing the risk of missing the RTO. Incremental backups (the best distractor) maximize storage efficiency but require restoring the full backup plus all subsequent incremental files, greatly increasing restoration time and RTO risk.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A new change is proposed to alter the access control list (ACL) of a highly sensitive database. Which two administrative controls must be completed in order to ensure both accountability and appropriate risk acceptance for this change?
Choices: A successful rollback test and validation of the system logs.
Formal documentation and approval in the Change Log.
Reviewing the change against the applicable security standard.
Requiring the Change Control Board (CCB) to perform the technical verification.
Questions.AnswerKey: Formal documentation and approval in the Change Log.
Questions.Explaination: The core of Change Management, particularly when dealing with risk, is ensuring managerial accountability. This is achieved by documenting the decision and formal approval (risk acceptance) in the Change Log. While successful testing is crucial, the Change Log is the authoritative record of the managerial decision and risk acceptance. Reviewing against the security standard is part of the preceding planning phase, not the final accountability step.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: Following the containment and recovery phases of a major intrusion, the Incident Commander must transition to long-term prevention. Which two distinct activities are required in the final stages of the IR life cycle to ensure process failures are documented and technical flaws are eliminated?
Choices: Mitigation (containment) and Reporting (notification).
Recovery (restoration) and Eradication (root cause fix).
Remediation (vulnerability patch) and Lessons Learned (process review).
Post-incident review and updating the BCP document.
Questions.AnswerKey: Remediation (vulnerability patch) and Lessons Learned (process review).
Questions.Explaination: The final stages of the CISSP IR life cycle are Remediation (fixing the technical root cause) and Lessons Learned (the formal administrative review to improve policies and processes). Recovery and Eradication (the best distractor) are part of the 'Response' phase and focus on immediate system restoration, not the final long-term process improvement steps.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A systems architect is designing a physical security solution for a top-secret research lab. The CISO mandates a redundant access system using biometric scanners, monitored by security guards. Which control classification pair BEST describes the intended function of the biometric scanner versus the security guard?
Choices: Biometric Scanner: Corrective; Security Guard: Detective.
Biometric Scanner: Preventive; Security Guard: Detective.
Biometric Scanner: Deterrent; Security Guard: Preventive.
Biometric Scanner: Compensating; Security Guard: Administrative.
Questions.AnswerKey: Biometric Scanner: Preventive; Security Guard: Detective.
Questions.Explaination: The biometric scanner actively enforces the access policy by physically denying unauthorized entry (Preventive control). The security guard monitors the area and notes unauthorized activity, which is the definition of a Detective control. The guard may also act as a Deterrent, but Detective is the guard's primary function when monitoring. Deterrent, the best distractor for the scanner, is incorrect because the scanner actively stops the violation, rather than just discouraging it.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The security team is preparing to test the organization’s Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP). Which testing methodology is MOST comprehensive for validating both the procedural efficacy of the plan and the team's ability to operate under realistic time pressure?
Choices: A parallel test, running production data at the alternate site while the primary site remains active.
A full interruption test, shutting down the primary site to force activation of the alternate facility.
A walkthrough exercise (tabletop) involving all technical and business stakeholders.
A simulation test, running a complex disaster scenario in a controlled environment.
Questions.AnswerKey: A full interruption test, shutting down the primary site to force activation of the alternate facility.
Questions.Explaination: The full interruption test (full-scale test) is the most comprehensive type of DRP test, as it requires deliberately shutting down the primary environment, forcing the full activation of the alternate site and testing the plan and personnel under realistic time constraints. A parallel test, the best distractor, is highly accurate as it uses production data but fails to test the switchover process itself because the primary site remains running.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A key encryption key must be protected while it is actively being used by the CPU for decryption operations. Which control goal is the MOST challenging to enforce during this phase of the data life cycle, and why?
Choices: Integrity, because the key is vulnerable to side-channel attacks during processing.
Confidentiality, because the key must exist in an unencrypted (plaintext) state in memory.
Availability, because the key is subject to loss if the system fails unexpectedly.
Non-repudiation, because the key usage cannot be logged or audited while in use.
Questions.AnswerKey: Confidentiality, because the key must exist in an unencrypted (plaintext) state in memory.
Questions.Explaination: Data in use (in memory) is the most challenging state to protect because the encryption key must be decrypted (in plaintext) to fulfill its function, inherently violating confidentiality within that volatile memory space [1]. The system is most vulnerable to memory scraping or related attacks here. Integrity and Availability are also concerns, but the fundamental challenge is the necessary exposure of the key in plaintext to the memory [1].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: An organization is migrating to a cloud-based identity management solution. They need assurance that the service provider’s technical security controls are continuously operating effectively. Which strategic administrative action is MOST appropriate for the CISO to maintain Due Diligence regarding the vendor’s performance?
Choices: Conducting monthly internal audits of the organization’s access control lists (ACLs).
Requiring the vendor to submit a full list of all security policies and procedures.
Contractually mandating continuous security monitoring (CSM) via NIST 800-137 compliance.
Requiring the vendor to provide annual external penetration test reports.
Questions.AnswerKey: Contractually mandating continuous security monitoring (CSM) via NIST 800-137 compliance.
Questions.Explaination: Due Diligence requires continuous oversight of controls. Mandating CSM ensures that the effectiveness of the security controls is being validated and reported on continuously, providing objective, ongoing data on the vendor's security posture. Annual penetration tests (the best distractor) provide only a point-in-time assessment, failing to meet the continuous oversight requirement. Requiring policies is part of initial Due Diligence but does not confirm operational effectiveness.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: When implementing access control to a highly sensitive database, a security manager ensures that every user is restricted to viewing only the data fields and records necessary for their specific job function, regardless of their overall system privileges. This is an enforcement of which two distinct access control principles?
Choices: Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Separation of Duties (SoD).
Mandatory Access Control (MAC) and Implicit Deny.
Principle of Least Privilege and Need-to-Know.
Two-person control and Confidentiality.
Questions.AnswerKey: Principle of Least Privilege and Need-to-Know.
Questions.Explaination: The Principle of Least Privilege is the overarching concept that users should have the minimum access necessary. Need-to-Know is the specific application of Least Privilege regarding sensitive data, limiting access only to the information required for the immediate task, making this pair the most accurate. RBAC (the best distractor) is the technical mechanism that often enforces Least Privilege, but the principle is the core concept being applied managerially.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A new administrative assistant is hired and provisioned. Which sequence of actions correctly follows the administrative process for granting access rights, ensuring security controls are applied before active system use?
Choices: Entitlement definition, account creation, privilege audit, access review.
Access review, Entitlement definition, account creation, activation.
Classification of data, Entitlement definition, activation, access review.
Entitlement definition, account creation, provisioning/allocation, activation.
Questions.AnswerKey: Entitlement definition, account creation, provisioning/allocation, activation.
Questions.Explaination: The provisioning life cycle requires defining the standard privileges for the role (Entitlement) [2], creating the account, then linking the account to the necessary resources/groups (provisioning/allocation), and finally enabling the account for use (activation). An access review occurs later in the life cycle, making it the primary distractor that represents an incorrect sequence.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The CISO requires a security operations center (SOC) to move from reactive detection to proactive threat identification against unknown attack vectors. Which strategic security intelligence activity MUST the SOC prioritize to achieve this proactive goal?
Choices: Implementing signature-based IPS rules based on open-source threat feeds.
Implementing User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) for anomaly hunting.
Ensuring all system clocks are synchronized via Network Time Protocol (NTP).
Contractually mandating third-party vulnerability assessments (VAs).
Questions.AnswerKey: Implementing User and Entity Behavior Analytics (UEBA) for anomaly hunting.
Questions.Explaination: Proactive threat identification against *unknown* (zero-day/novel) threats requires analyzing deviations from the norm, which is the core function of UEBA and anomaly detection [3]. Signature-based systems (the best distractor) are reactive and only detect *known* threats. NTP synchronization is foundational for forensic integrity but is not a method for proactive threat hunting.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The security team is performing a full forensic investigation on a server involved in a breach. After the initial collection of volatile data, which sequence of administrative and technical steps is mandatory to maintain legal admissibility and data integrity of the subsequent hard drive image?
Choices: Calculate the cryptographic hash, initiate the Chain of Custody (COC), and then analyze the data.
Initiate the COC, calculate the cryptographic hash, and then store the image securely.
Store the image on WORM media, document the scene, and then calculate the hash.
Analyze the data, report findings to management, and then store the image securely.
Questions.AnswerKey: Initiate the COC, calculate the cryptographic hash, and then store the image securely.
Questions.Explaination: The Chain of Custody (COC) must be initiated immediately upon seizure to document legal handling. The cryptographic hash calculation (technical integrity proof) must occur next, immediately after the image is created, and before secure storage. Analyzing the data and reporting findings (the best distractor) occur much later in the forensic process [4].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A global company experiences an active ransomware attack that has spread rapidly across multiple regions. After containing the attack, the Incident Commander must prioritize the next two managerial actions to ensure compliance and minimize liability.
Choices: Notify law enforcement and initiate the technical remediation (root cause fix).
Restore systems from clean backups (Recovery) and conduct post-incident review.
Notify regulatory bodies and key stakeholders, followed by verifying all service continuity plans.
Collect all volatile evidence (forensics) and ensure all server clocks are synchronized (NTP).
Questions.AnswerKey: Notify regulatory bodies and key stakeholders, followed by verifying all service continuity plans.
Questions.Explaination: Following containment, the immediate managerial priority is Reporting to fulfill legal/regulatory notification requirements (e.g., GDPR, state laws), thus minimizing liability. This is immediately followed by initiating the Recovery phase, which includes verifying that service continuity plans are ready to support restoration. Initiating technical remediation (the best distractor) is crucial but follows reporting and recovery in the managerial priority sequence.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A data owner classifies a new financial transaction data set as 'Confidential.' Which necessary step in the data life cycle must be performed immediately after this classification decision to ensure proper protection throughout the rest of the cycle?
Choices: Determine the mandatory data retention period and disposal mechanism.
Encrypting the data using AES-256 for storage and transit.
Assigning an appropriate security label to the data set.
Ensuring the data is backed up to geographically dispersed hot sites.
Questions.AnswerKey: Assigning an appropriate security label to the data set.
Questions.Explaination: Once data is classified, the next mandatory step is labeling the data [5]. Labeling ensures that all subsequent users, systems, and processes (including encryption tools, access controls, and retention policies) correctly identify and apply the appropriate security controls based on the sensitivity level [5, 6]. Encryption is a technical control resulting from the label, making it the next logical step but not the immediate process following classification.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The physical security team is installing electronic turnstiles at the main entrance and requires them to lock down (deny access) if tampering or system failure is detected. This design choice is made to ensure access control integrity. Which two principles does this configuration satisfy, and why is the alternative unacceptable?
Choices: Satisfies: Fail Securely and Defense in Depth; Unacceptable Alternative: Fail Open (due to asset risk).
Satisfies: Protection of Life Safety and Least Privilege; Unacceptable Alternative: Fail Securely (due to human safety).
Satisfies: Least Privilege and Implicit Deny; Unacceptable Alternative: Trust but Verify (due to lack of trust).
Satisfies: Fail Open and Deterrence; Unacceptable Alternative: Fail Securely (due to compliance risk).
Questions.AnswerKey: Satisfies: Fail Securely and Defense in Depth; Unacceptable Alternative: Fail Open (due to asset risk).
Questions.Explaination: The primary intent is asset protection (locking down) upon failure, which is the definition of Fail Securely. The unacceptable alternative is Fail Open, which would compromise asset protection (allowing unauthorized entry), leading to unacceptable asset risk. Life Safety is not involved at the main entrance turnstile as it is not an egress point, making that choice an incorrect managerial priority for this context.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A company requires its most sensitive financial transaction system to maintain the highest level of availability and data synchronization, aiming for a near-zero Recovery Point Objective (RPO) and RTO. Which recovery site solution BEST achieves this stringent goal, and which DRP resource is LEAST necessary?
Choices: Cold site; least necessary is pre-installed hardware.
Hot site; least necessary is large stockpiles of fuel.
Warm site; least necessary is extensive data synchronization technology.
Redundant site; least necessary is dedicated business personnel.
Questions.AnswerKey: Hot site; least necessary is large stockpiles of fuel.
Questions.Explaination: Hot sites or Redundant sites provide the lowest RTO/RPO via full synchronization and immediate operational readiness. If the facility is highly available and relies on real-time replication and quick failover (which a Hot Site provides), long-term operational resources like large stockpiles of generator fuel are less critical than immediate synchronization and hardware availability. Fuel reserves are essential for extended operation, but immediate recovery is the priority.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The security manager is implementing a power continuity strategy for a primary data center with a low RTO. To compensate for both short-term utility fluctuations and regional outages lasting up to 48 hours, which redundant infrastructure elements must be deployed?
Choices: Redundant Power Distribution Units (PDUs) and georedundant cold sites.
Dual Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPS) and sufficient fuel reserves for the generator.
Mandatory RPO of zero and continuous offsite backup tape rotation.
Separated power grids (utility diversity) and a second hot site subscription.
Questions.AnswerKey: Dual Uninterruptible Power Supplies (UPS) and sufficient fuel reserves for the generator.
Questions.Explaination: Short-term fluctuations are mitigated by UPS (power conditioning and bridge power). Long-term outages (48 hours) require a generator, which necessitates sufficient fuel reserves for sustained operation. This combination directly addresses both short-term and extended power loss risks. Redundant PDUs (the best distractor) are necessary for distribution integrity but cannot provide power sustainment during an outage.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: Which security principle, when ignored, results in the administrative failure known as privilege creep, and what is the primary operational procedure required to correct this failure?
Choices: Violated Principle: Separation of Duties (SoD); Correction: Job Rotation.
Violated Principle: Fail Securely; Correction: Regular DRP testing.
Violated Principle: Principle of Least Privilege; Correction: User Access Reviews (UARs).
Violated Principle: Need-to-Know; Correction: Continuous monitoring (CSM).
Questions.AnswerKey: Violated Principle: Principle of Least Privilege; Correction: User Access Reviews (UARs).
Questions.Explaination: Privilege creep violates the Principle of Least Privilege (user has more access than needed). The designated administrative control to detect and remediate this failure during operations is the periodic User Access Review (UAR). Job Rotation (the best distractor) is a control intended to prevent fraud and cross-train staff, but UARs are specifically for verifying entitlements against current roles.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The security manager is integrating a new intrusion detection tool that monitors network traffic and flags events based on a statistical baseline of 'normal' user activity, rather than predefined attack signatures. Which two control characteristics best classify this tool's primary security function?
Choices: Detective control and Signature-based analysis.
Detective control and Anomaly detection.
Preventive control and Heuristic analysis.
Corrective control and Knowledge-based detection.
Questions.AnswerKey: Detective control and Anomaly detection.
Questions.Explaination: The tool monitors and flags activity (Detective control). The method of identifying activity based on statistical deviations from a baseline is Anomaly detection (or heuristic analysis). Signature-based analysis, the best distractor, is incorrect because the tool is specifically described as looking beyond predefined attack signatures.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: A third-party contractor requires temporary administrative access to patch a critical application. To comply with the Principle of Least Privilege and maintain the highest level of accountability, which access control mechanism MUST be used?
Choices: Standard Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) with supervisor oversight.
Mandatory two-person control with continuous audit logging.
Just-in-Time (JIT) access provisioned for the specific task and time frame.
Time-of-day restrictions coupled with geo-fencing policies.
Questions.AnswerKey: Just-in-Time (JIT) access provisioned for the specific task and time frame.
Questions.Explaination: JIT access is the most effective technical mechanism to enforce Least Privilege dynamically, ensuring the elevated permissions are revoked immediately after the task/time frame expires. While two-person control (the best distractor) enforces accountability for the task execution, JIT is superior in limiting the *duration* of the high privilege, thereby minimizing the attack surface associated with the temporary contractor access.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: When decommissioning magnetic hard drives containing PII that must remain unrecoverable by standard software recovery tools, the security manager mandates overwriting the media with random data. Which security level is achieved by this method, and which legal mandate is it typically sufficient to satisfy?
Choices: Achieved: Purging; Satisfied: Legal Hold requirements.
Achieved: Clearing; Satisfied: General internal reuse policies.
Achieved: Destruction; Satisfied: Absolute forensic unrecoverability.
Achieved: Clearing; Satisfied: Compliance with most PII disposal regulations.
Questions.AnswerKey: Achieved: Clearing; Satisfied: General internal reuse policies.
Questions.Explaination: Overwriting with random data achieves Clearing, making the data unrecoverable by common disk utility software. This level is sufficient for media that will be reused internally in a less sensitive context. Purging (the best distractor) requires a more intensive process (like degaussing or more comprehensive overwriting) to resist forensic laboratory recovery, which is a higher security requirement than stated here.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The CISO is evaluating a vendor that handles internal data. The CISO receives a SOC 1 Type II report and a SOC 2 Type II report. Based solely on the CISO's need for assurance regarding system security and operational effectiveness, which report is MOST relevant, and why?
Choices: SOC 1 Type II, because the 'Type II' designation validates control effectiveness over time.
SOC 2 Type II, because it specifically covers security, integrity, and availability controls.
SOC 1 Type II, because it focuses on internal controls over financial reporting.
SOC 2 Type II, because the 'Type I' designation is insufficient for external vendor review.
Questions.AnswerKey: SOC 2 Type II, because it specifically covers security, integrity, and availability controls.
Questions.Explaination: The SOC 2 report specifically addresses security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy controls, making it the most relevant report for assessing a vendor's security posture. The Type II further confirms the effectiveness over time. SOC 1 (the best distractor) is less relevant because its primary focus is internal controls over financial reporting, not security controls, despite having the required Type II time component.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The Crisis Management Team is developing a communications strategy for dealing with a major service outage. Which managerial priority dictates that all external communication efforts be standardized and prepared in advance?
Choices: Ensuring the legal admissibility of forensic evidence.
Minimizing reputational damage and maintaining public trust.
Reducing the Recovery Time Objective (RTO) for affected services.
Adhering to the Prudent Man Rule for senior management accountability.
Questions.AnswerKey: Minimizing reputational damage and maintaining public trust.
Questions.Explaination: Crisis communication (a key element of the BCP) is primarily focused on managing external perceptions, minimizing reputational damage, and maintaining public trust, which are top managerial priorities [7]. The Prudent Man Rule (the best distractor) applies to senior executive accountability for exercising Due Care, but minimizing reputation damage is the direct objective of the communication strategy itself.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: When implementing data backup processes, the operational efficiency is best described by the tradeoff between data storage size and restoration complexity. Which two backup types represent the extreme ends of this tradeoff spectrum?
Choices: Full backups (high size, low complexity) and Differential backups (moderate size, low complexity).
Incremental backups (low size, high complexity) and Full backups (high size, low complexity).
Incremental backups (low size, high complexity) and Differential backups (high size, high complexity).
Differential backups (moderate size, moderate complexity) and Transaction logs (very low size, high complexity).
Questions.AnswerKey: Incremental backups (low size, high complexity) and Full backups (high size, low complexity).
Questions.Explaination: Full backups require the most storage but are the simplest to restore (one file). Incremental backups require the least storage daily but are the most complex to restore (requiring the full plus every subsequent incremental file). These represent the extremes. Differential backups (the close distractor) fall in the middle: higher size than incremental but lower complexity than incremental.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The CISO is asked to review the security architecture for a new medical records system. Due to the high sensitivity of the Protected Health Information (PHI) and the mandatory nature of security controls, which access control model should the CISO mandate, as it is based on classification and system-defined policy, rather than user discretion?
Choices: Discretionary Access Control (DAC)
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Mandatory Access Control (MAC)
Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)
Questions.AnswerKey: Mandatory Access Control (MAC)
Questions.Explaination: Mandatory Access Control (MAC) is based on explicit data classification labels and strict system rules, enforcing access based on the security level of the subject and the object, rather than the user's discretion. MAC is often used in high-security environments (government, military) where control over high-sensitivity data (like PHI) is paramount. RBAC, the best distractor, is a non-discretionary model widely used in commercial settings, but it is based on functional roles rather than strict security classification levels, making MAC superior for high-sensitivity data where policy must override all else [8].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: An organization is deploying a new Incident Response policy based on the CISSP seven-step model. Which sequence of activities accurately describes the movement from identifying the threat to minimizing its scope?
Choices: Detection, Mitigation, Response, Reporting.
Detection, Response, Mitigation, Reporting.
Response, Mitigation, Recovery, Remediation.
Detection, Triage, Containment, Eradication.
Questions.AnswerKey: Detection, Response, Mitigation, Reporting.
Questions.Explaination: The CISSP seven-step IR process is Detect, Response, Mitigate (Containment), Report, Recover, Remediate, and Lessons Learned. Detection identifies the incident, Response activates the team, and Mitigation contains/limits the scope. Response and Mitigation are often performed concurrently, but Mitigation formally follows Response in the documented sequence [9]. Detection, Triage, Containment, Eradication (the best distractor) uses terms from other models (like SANS/NIST) and doesn't align with the strict CISSP sequence.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: The security manager must ensure that the organization’s overall security program adheres to Due Care. Which strategic activity is the most appropriate way to periodically confirm that the technical controls are actually implemented and operating as intended?
Choices: Conducting monthly management reviews of the Security Policy compliance metrics.
Facilitating annual third-party security audits of the implemented controls.
Mandating bi-weekly technical vulnerability assessments across the infrastructure.
Ensuring that all new security systems adhere to the Secure Defaults principle.
Questions.AnswerKey: Facilitating annual third-party security audits of the implemented controls.
Questions.Explaination: Due Care is demonstrated by performing reasonable actions (the doing). An external (third-party) audit provides an unbiased, formal assessment that verifies controls are implemented and operating correctly, giving the highest level of assurance to management that Due Care is being exercised. Conducting vulnerability assessments (the best distractor) is a good operational task but is not the formal validation of the *entire security program* that an audit provides [10].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: An organization relies on two distinct servers for application processing, each with an MTBF of 1,000 hours and an MTTR of 1 hour. To achieve 99.99% availability, the security manager decides to use clustering to distribute the workload. This strategic design decision is BEST characterized as a direct application of which two security concepts?
Choices: Least Privilege and Economy of Mechanism.
High Availability and Redundancy.
Separation of Duties and Trust but Verify.
Fault Tolerance and Confidentiality.
Questions.AnswerKey: High Availability and Redundancy.
Questions.Explaination: Clustering two servers to distribute workload is a form of Redundancy (using multiple components) designed to enhance the overall High Availability (HA) of the service, ensuring service uptime meets the goal (99.99%). Fault Tolerance, the closest distractor, is a similar concept but strictly implies zero service interruption, while clustering and HA often involve brief failover latency during a component failure. Redundancy is the mechanism used to achieve the HA goal.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 7: Security Operations
Questions.Question: To reduce the risk associated with a third-party vendor handling proprietary business data, the CISO requires a legal agreement that explicitly defines the consequences, including penalties and liability, should the data be disclosed without authorization. Which legal agreement is MOST crucial for addressing this managerial risk exposure?
Choices: Service Level Agreement (SLA) defining uptime and availability penalties.
Master Services Agreement (MSA) defining the scope of work.
Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) with strict liability clauses.
Business Associate Agreement (BAA) for HIPAA compliance.
Questions.AnswerKey: Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) with strict liability clauses.
Questions.Explaination: The primary risk being managed is the unauthorized disclosure of proprietary data. The Non-Disclosure Agreement (NDA) is the legal tool that specifically establishes confidentiality requirements and outlines financial and legal penalties (liability) for data disclosure. An SLA (the best distractor) focuses on service performance (availability and uptime), not the liability associated with data confidentiality breach.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What traditional Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model is prioritized when clear objectives and stability are needed, often favored for systems affecting human safety or highly stable requirements?
Choices: Agile
Spiral
DevOps
Waterfall
Questions.AnswerKey: Waterfall
Questions.Explaination: The Waterfall model remains appropriate when requirements are clear, stable, and well-documented from the outset, especially in systems where preventing flaws (like those affecting human safety) is prioritized over speed, stability, and cost [1, 1-3]. Agile (the close distractor) and DevOps prioritize iterative development and speed, which are less suitable when high control and fixed requirements are paramount [1].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which type of application attack exploits flaws in input validation to force the system to navigate outside the intended directory structure to access unauthorized files, such as configuration files?
Choices: Directory Traversal
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
Command Injection
Brute Force Attack
Questions.AnswerKey: Directory Traversal
Questions.Explaination: Directory Traversal attacks use specific character strings (like '..') to move up the file hierarchy to access restricted files [1, 4]. Command Injection (the close distractor) is a similar input validation flaw, but it specifically targets the execution of OS commands, not unauthorized file system navigation [1, 4, 5].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which type of code analysis is conducted without executing the program, primarily utilizing automated tools or human code reviews to analyze the source code structure and logic?
Choices: Fuzzing
Dynamic Testing
Static Program Analysis
Regression Testing
Questions.AnswerKey: Static Program Analysis
Questions.Explaination: Static Program Analysis involves examining source code without execution [6, 7]. Dynamic Testing (the close distractor) is the opposing methodology, which involves executing the program with various inputs to check performance and behavior [7, 8].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: In the Software Capability Maturity Model (SW-CMM), what is the highest level, characterized by continuous process improvement driven by quantitative feedback loops?
Choices: Managed
Defined
Optimized
Repeatable
Questions.AnswerKey: Optimized
Questions.Explaination: The Optimized level (Level 5) represents the highest maturity, focusing on continuous improvement and evolutionary changes. Managed (Level 4), the close distractor, is high maturity but focuses on quantitative measurement to understand results, while Optimized focuses on using those results to drive continuous process improvement [3, 9].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What specific countermeasure is used to increase the complexity of dictionary and brute-force password attacks by adding random data to the password before hashing?
Choices: Parameterization
Cryptographic salts
Key stretching
Input validation
Questions.AnswerKey: Cryptographic salts
Questions.Explaination: Cryptographic salts are random data added to a password before hashing to prevent rainbow table attacks and slow down brute-force attempts [10, 11]. Key stretching is a related technique that increases the processing time required for a hash calculation, but 'salts' are the random data component used to ensure unique hashes even for identical passwords [10].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What code testing methodology operates by executing the program code with various inputs to check its behavior, performance, and security flaws during runtime?
Choices: Static Testing
Code Review
Dynamic Testing
White Box Testing
Questions.AnswerKey: Dynamic Testing
Questions.Explaination: Dynamic testing involves running the code and observing its output and behavior in response to inputs [7, 8]. Static Testing (the close distractor) examines the code without execution [6, 7]. White Box Testing often includes both dynamic and static analysis when the tester has full knowledge of the source code [7].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What is the most prevalent application attack where malicious Structured Query Language (SQL) statements are inserted into an input field for execution by the back-end database?
Choices: Directory Traversal
Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
SQL Injection
Buffer Overflow
Questions.AnswerKey: SQL Injection
Questions.Explaination: SQL Injection is a common application attack that exploits input validation flaws to allow attackers to execute arbitrary SQL commands [12-14]. Directory Traversal (the close distractor) also exploits input flaws but specifically targets the file system navigation [1].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What secure design principle mandates that the default configuration of a system should reflect a restrictive or conservative enforcement of the security policy upon installation?
Choices: Secure Defaults
Fail Securely
Defense in Depth
Principle of Least Privilege
Questions.AnswerKey: Secure Defaults
Questions.Explaination: The Secure Defaults principle ensures that systems start in the most restrictive state possible, denying access rather than granting it [4, 15, 16]. Fail Securely (the close distractor) is the principle dictating how a system should respond *after* a component fails (by denying access), rather than defining the initial configuration [4, 15].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What basic secure coding practice involves checking all user-supplied data to ensure it adheres to predefined constraints, such as required type, length, and format, before processing?
Choices: Parameterization
Error handling
Input validation
Code obfuscation
Questions.AnswerKey: Input validation
Questions.Explaination: Input validation is the crucial step of inspecting and sanitizing user data to ensure it meets expectations and prevents malicious input from causing security flaws [7, 11, 12]. Parameterization (the close distractor) is a specific technique for implementing security during database calls, often used as a direct countermeasure to SQL injection [12].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What is the inventory of all proprietary and open-source building blocks, libraries, and versions used in a software product, required for managing supply chain risk?
Choices: Source Code Repository
Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
Integrated Development Environment (IDE)
Continuous Integration/Continuous Delivery (CI/CD)
Questions.AnswerKey: Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)
Questions.Explaination: The SBOM is an inventory of the components (building blocks) that make up a software product, allowing organizations to understand, manage, and secure their applications by tracking vulnerabilities in dependencies [17, 18]. The Source Code Repository (the close distractor) is where the source code is stored, but it is not the formal inventory of third-party components [17].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What software development methodology integrates development and IT operations to automate and monitor processes, focusing on rapid and reliable deployment?
Choices: Agile
Waterfall
DevOps
Spiral
Questions.AnswerKey: DevOps
Questions.Explaination: DevOps is the methodology emphasizing the automation of the software delivery process, often encompassing Continuous Integration (CI) and Continuous Delivery (CD) practices [1, 3]. Agile (the close distractor) is a preceding methodology focused on iterative development and customer feedback, which DevOps builds upon.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What secure coding practice ensures that sensitive system information, such as stack traces or internal configuration details, is not displayed to users when an application encounters a failure?
Choices: Session management
Error handling and logging
Communication security
Input validation
Questions.AnswerKey: Error handling and logging
Questions.Explaination: Error handling and logging is the secure coding practice that prevents sensitive information from being disclosed in error responses [19]. Session management (the close distractor) is used to protect user state and identity, not specifically the disclosure of back-end error details.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What term describes the creation, maintenance, and deactivation of user objects and their access attributes as they exist in one or more systems in response to business processes?
Choices: Entitlement management
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Access review
User provisioning
Questions.AnswerKey: User provisioning
Questions.Explaination: User provisioning refers to the entire lifecycle process of creating, maintaining, and deactivating user identities and their accounts [20]. Entitlement management (the close distractor) is the specific process of defining the rights and privileges assigned to a user during provisioning.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which access control principle specifically limits a subject’s access to only the data objects essential for performing their current job function, regardless of overall system privileges?
Choices: Separation of Duties (SoD)
Principle of Least Privilege
Need-to-Know
Mandatory Access Control (MAC)
Questions.AnswerKey: Need-to-Know
Questions.Explaination: The Need-to-Know principle is the administrative control that focuses the Principle of Least Privilege specifically on data access, ensuring users only view necessary information [21, 22]. Principle of Least Privilege (the close distractor) is the overarching rule that mandates minimum rights for all resources, systems, and data [4, 22-25].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What phenomenon occurs when employees accumulate unnecessary access rights over time due to transferring roles, violating the Principle of Least Privilege?
Choices: Unauthorized access
Account takeover
Privilege creep
Role ambiguity
Questions.AnswerKey: Privilege creep
Questions.Explaination: Privilege creep is the direct result of access rights accumulating over years due to held positions or role changes where older permissions were not revoked [11, 22-24, 26]. Unauthorized access (the close distractor) is a broader term that applies to any access without permission, while privilege creep is a specific, organizational failure of the access management process [22].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What type of technical security control is used in the data life cycle to control how data is utilized, often defining restrictions on operations like copying, printing, or transferring data?
Choices: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Data Rights Management (DRM)
Homomorphic Encryption
Questions.AnswerKey: Data Rights Management (DRM)
Questions.Explaination: Data Rights Management (DRM) is a security mechanism that controls how data is used after it has been distributed (e.g., restricting copying, printing, or viewing duration) [27, 28]. Data Loss Prevention (DLP) is a system that enforces policy and monitors data movement, making it the technical detective/preventive tool that supports the DRM policy [28].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: In the Software Capability Maturity Model (SW-CMM), what is the lowest level, characterized by ad hoc, chaotic processes with results highly dependent on individual effort and ability?
Choices: Repeatable
Defined
Managed
Initial (or Ad Hoc)
Questions.AnswerKey: Initial (or Ad Hoc)
Questions.Explaination: The Initial (Level 1) or Ad Hoc state is the least mature, where processes are unorganized and chaotic [3]. Repeatable (Level 2), the close distractor, is the next level where basic project management processes are implemented, allowing success to be repeated [3].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What term describes the action of making information obscure, unclear, or unintelligible, often by hiding sensitive data in a complex structure to conceal its meaning?
Choices: Confidentiality
Encryption
Obfuscation
Steganography
Questions.AnswerKey: Obfuscation
Questions.Explaination: Obfuscation is the general action of intentionally making something difficult to understand or perceive, which serves to hide information [28]. Encryption (the close distractor) is a specific, mathematical technique used to achieve obfuscation and confidentiality [28].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Data that is actively being processed, residing in CPU registers, or stored in volatile Random Access Memory (RAM) during computation is categorized as which type?
Choices: Data at rest
Data in motion
Data in use
Data in transit
Questions.AnswerKey: Data in use
Questions.Explaination: Data in use refers to data actively being used in computational activity, typically residing in memory or CPU registers, which is the most challenging state to protect because it must be decrypted [28-30]. Data at rest (the close distractor) refers to data stored on persistent storage like hard drives or tapes [27, 30].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which approach to threat modeling focuses on developing countermeasures and prioritizing mitigation efforts based on the financial and business value of the affected assets?
Choices: Focused on assets
Focused on attackers
STRIDE
Trike
Questions.AnswerKey: Focused on assets
Questions.Explaination: Asset-focused threat modeling uses asset valuation (monetary or business value) to drive threat identification and countermeasure prioritization [31, 32]. Attacker-focused models (the close distractor) center on the goals and tactics of external adversaries, which is different from valuing the asset itself [31, 32].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What Microsoft-developed threat modeling technique uses a mnemonic to focus on software-related threats, including Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, and Elevation of privileges?
Choices: PASTA
STRIDE
DREAD
Attack Trees
Questions.AnswerKey: STRIDE
Questions.Explaination: STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, and Elevation of privileges) is the mnemonic developed by Microsoft for categorizing software threats [33, 34]. PASTA is an alternative methodology that focuses on asset value and developing countermeasures [32].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: According to the Common Criteria Evaluation Assurance Levels (EALs), which level indicates that the Target of Evaluation (TOE) has only been functionally tested?
Choices: EAL4
EAL1
EAL7
EAL3
Questions.AnswerKey: EAL1
Questions.Explaination: EAL1 is the lowest level of assurance and means the system has only undergone functional testing, confirming basic functionality without extensive security focus [24, 35]. EAL3, the close distractor, involves methodical design, testing, and review, providing a much higher level of assurance [24, 36].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which character string is characteristic of a directory traversal attack, used by attackers to reference a directory one level higher in the file hierarchy?
Choices: A single forward slash (/)
Two periods (..)
A backslash (\)
An ampersand (&)
Questions.AnswerKey: Two periods (..)
Questions.Explaination: The string '..' (two periods followed by a directory separator) is the key indicator of a directory traversal attempt, as it instructs the file system to move up one level in the directory structure [1, 4]. A single forward slash (/) refers to the root directory, which is non-malicious in this context.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What concept refers to the level of confidence an organization has that its security controls are properly implemented and effective in meeting security requirements?
Choices: Verification
Assurance
Accreditation
Certification
Questions.AnswerKey: Assurance
Questions.Explaination: Assurance represents the level of confidence an organization holds that its controls are correctly implemented and effective, a confidence that must be regularly monitored and verified [24]. Verification and Certification are processes often used to provide this confidence (assurance), but Assurance is the confidence level itself [24, 35].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Data that is stored physically on hard drives, backup tapes, or other non-volatile storage media is known by which term?
Choices: Data in transit
Data in motion
Data at rest
Data in use
Questions.AnswerKey: Data at rest
Questions.Explaination: Data at rest refers to data stored on any kind of persistent media [27, 30]. Data in motion (or in transit), the close distractor, refers to data actively moving across a network [30].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What secure coding technique involves using placeholders or parameters rather than directly embedding user input into database queries to prevent SQL injection attacks?
Choices: Input validation
Escaping special characters
Parameterization
Error handling
Questions.AnswerKey: Parameterization
Questions.Explaination: Parameterization (using prepared statements) ensures that user input is treated only as data, not as executable code, directly preventing injection attacks [12]. Escaping special characters (the close distractor) is a related technique for input sanitization but is less robust against complex injection than parameterization [12].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What is typically utilized by developers to restrict access to Application Programming Interfaces (APIs) for authorized users and applications, often used for both authentication and authorization?
Choices: Secure Shell (SSH)
API keys
SOAP protocol
JSON Web Tokens (JWTs)
Questions.AnswerKey: API keys
Questions.Explaination: API keys are long, complex values primarily used for authentication and authorization to control access to APIs [1, 37]. JWTs (the close distractor) are often used in conjunction with APIs to transfer claims and session information securely, but the key itself is the primary access credential [1].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which type of firewall is designed to protect web applications specifically from application-layer threats like SQL injection, cross-site scripting, and buffer overflows?
Choices: Next Generation Firewall (NGFW)
Static packet filtering firewall
Web Application Firewall (WAF)
Stateful inspection firewall
Questions.AnswerKey: Web Application Firewall (WAF)
Questions.Explaination: A Web Application Firewall (WAF) is an application-level firewall designed to protect web apps from threats listed in the OWASP Top 10 [1, 38]. An NGFW (the close distractor) also inspects traffic at the application layer but is a broader network firewall focused on protocols and deep packet inspection across the entire network perimeter [38].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Why is client-side input validation considered an unreliable defense against application injection attacks?
Choices: Client-side validation requires excessive processing power on the server.
The client-side code can be easily modified or bypassed by an attacker.
It makes the application development process too complex.
It introduces too many potential false positives.
Questions.AnswerKey: The client-side code can be easily modified or bypassed by an attacker.
Questions.Explaination: Client-side input validation is considered an unreliable defense against injection attacks because it operates within the client's system, where an attacker can easily modify the client-side code or bypass it entirely to send unauthorized or malicious data directly to the server [1-3]. Therefore, contrary to server-side validation, client-side validation may be bypassed and effectively rendered useless [2]. When aiming to prevent injection attacks (like SQL injection), the CISSP standard dictates that server-side input validation is the mandatory defense, ensuring the web application never trusts outside data input and validates the data before it passes to the database [4-7]. If client-side validation is used, it must be emphatically complemented by server-side validation [7].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: In the context of the STRIDE threat model, what type of attack has occurred when an attacker manages to transform a limited user account into one with higher privileges?
Choices: Spoofing
Repudiation
Elevation of Privileges
Tampering
Questions.AnswerKey: Elevation of Privileges
Questions.Explaination: Elevation of Privileges (EoP) attacks occur when a limited user exploits a vulnerability to gain higher access rights [33, 34]. Repudiation (the close distractor) refers to an actor denying responsibility for an action [39].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What concept refers to a group of systems working together to handle shared workloads, often utilizing a load balancer to manage incoming traffic, enhancing availability?
Choices: Redundancy
Clustering
Fault Tolerance
High Availability (HA)
Questions.AnswerKey: Clustering
Questions.Explaination: Clustering specifically refers to multiple systems working together to handle workloads [40]. Redundancy (the close distractor) is the general principle of duplicating components; while clustering utilizes redundancy, 'clustering' is the specific term for the active workload-sharing configuration [40].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which traditional software development model is characterized by strictly sequential phases, where formal sign-off is required before moving to the next stage, making it ideal for high-assurance systems with fixed requirements?
Choices: Spiral Model
Agile Methodology
Waterfall Model
DevOps Integration
Questions.AnswerKey: Waterfall Model
Questions.Explaination: The Waterfall Model follows a rigid, linear approach where each phase must be completed before the next begins, providing high control and predictability, which is often preferred for high-assurance systems [1, 2]. The Agile Methodology, the best distractor, is based on iterative and flexible development cycles, which contrasts sharply with the strict sequential nature of Waterfall.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: An application attack involves inserting unauthorized commands into an input field, manipulating the database structure, and potentially extracting, modifying, or deleting sensitive back-end records. What type of injection vulnerability is this?
Choices: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
OS Command Injection
Directory Traversal
SQL Injection
Questions.AnswerKey: SQL Injection
Questions.Explaination: SQL Injection attacks specifically exploit flaws in input validation to inject malicious SQL queries directly into the application's database backend, allowing attackers to manipulate or exfiltrate data [3]. Cross-Site Scripting (XSS), the best distractor, also exploits input flaws, but its goal is to inject client-side scripts into the victim's browser, rather than targeting the backend database itself [4].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What Microsoft-developed threat modeling mnemonic is used to categorize application security flaws based on violation of the CIA triad and accountability principles, including Tampering and Information Disclosure?
Choices: PASTA
DREAD
Attack Trees
STRIDE
Questions.AnswerKey: STRIDE
Questions.Explaination: STRIDE (Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, and Elevation of privileges) is the formalized threat classification model used in application security [5-7]. DREAD, the best distractor, is a related risk ranking model (Damage, Reproducibility, Exploitability, Affected users, Discoverability) often used after STRIDE to quantify the severity of the identified threats [8].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Data residing on persistent storage media, such as hard drives or backup tapes, falls into which categorization within the secure data life cycle, typically protected by controls like whole-disk encryption?
Choices: Data in motion
Data in transit
Data in use
Data at rest
Questions.AnswerKey: Data at rest
Questions.Explaination: Data at rest is the state of data stored on non-volatile media, such as hard drives or tapes, and is typically protected by persistent controls like encryption [9]. Data in use (the best distractor) refers to data actively residing in memory (RAM) or CPU registers during processing [9].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which fundamental access control principle dictates that subjects (users or processes) are granted only the minimum set of permissions necessary to perform their legitimate job function, and nothing more?
Choices: Separation of Duties (SoD)
Need-to-Know
Principle of Least Privilege
Implicit Deny
Questions.AnswerKey: Principle of Least Privilege
Questions.Explaination: The Principle of Least Privilege is the overarching security principle mandating that users and processes receive only the necessary permissions to perform their duties, reducing the attack surface and potential damage from compromise [10-12]. Need-to-Know (the close distractor) is the administrative enforcement of Least Privilege specifically applied to restricting access to sensitive data [11, 13, 14].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which secure coding practice is implemented to prevent an application from exposing sensitive back-end diagnostic information, such as stack trace contents or database connection strings, to end-users during a failure?
Choices: Session management
Input validation
Error handling and logging
Output encoding
Questions.AnswerKey: Error handling and logging
Questions.Explaination: Proper error handling and logging is the secure coding practice that prevents unnecessary disclosure of technical and system details that could aid an attacker during an unexpected application failure [15, 16]. Output encoding (the close distractor) is used to prevent injection flaws (like XSS) in content displayed to users, not necessarily the sensitive information contained in error responses.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: In the Software Capability Maturity Model (SW-CMM), what maturity level describes an organization where processes are chaotic, poorly controlled, and success relies heavily on the heroic efforts of individual developers?
Choices: Repeatable (Level 2)
Managed (Level 4)
Initial (Level 1)
Defined (Level 3)
Questions.AnswerKey: Initial (Level 1)
Questions.Explaination: Level 1, or Initial (Ad Hoc), is the lowest maturity level where processes are disorganized and unpredictable, and success is not repeatable [17]. Repeatable (Level 2), the next level and best distractor, involves the introduction of basic project management processes, allowing historical success to be somewhat replicated, but still lacks standardized definitions [17].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What term describes the process of overwriting storage media multiple times with non-sensitive data to render previous information unrecoverable by standard software recovery tools, often applied when media is reused internally?
Choices: Purging
Degaussing
Clearing
Physical Destruction
Questions.AnswerKey: Clearing
Questions.Explaination: Clearing involves overwriting data using software or hardware methods to render it unrecoverable by common recovery tools, and it is suitable when the media remains within the organization and is reused [18]. Purging (the best distractor) is a higher level of sanitization designed to resist advanced forensic laboratory recovery efforts [18].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which common failure of access management occurs when an employee moves to a new role but retains unnecessary permissions from their previous position, leading to an expansion of unauthorized privileges?
Choices: Role ambiguity
Account review failure
Session hijacking
Privilege creep
Questions.AnswerKey: Privilege creep
Questions.Explaination: Privilege creep is the direct accumulation of access rights over time that violates the Principle of Least Privilege [10, 11]. Account review failure (the close distractor) is the administrative process failure that *allows* privilege creep to go undetected, but the phenomenon itself is privilege creep.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which cloud service model provides consumers with a managed environment and operating system platform upon which they can deploy, manage, and run their custom applications, while the provider manages the underlying infrastructure?
Choices: Software as a Service (SaaS)
Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
Platform as a Service (PaaS)
Function as a Service (FaaS)
Questions.AnswerKey: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
Questions.Explaination: Platform as a Service (PaaS) provides the customer with the environment (OS, runtime, necessary databases) to deploy their applications, managing the infrastructure below the operating system layer [19]. Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS), the close distractor, provides raw compute and storage infrastructure, requiring the customer to manage the operating system and above [19].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What software testing methodology is performed by analyzing the source code structure, logic, and control flow without actually executing the application?
Choices: Fuzzing
Dynamic Testing
Code Review
Static Program Analysis
Questions.AnswerKey: Static Program Analysis
Questions.Explaination: Static Program Analysis (or Static Testing) is conducted offline, examining the source code typically using automated tools to find flaws, complexity issues, and security vulnerabilities [20, 21]. Code Review (the close distractor) is a manual form of static testing, but Static Program Analysis is the general category of automated, non-execution testing [20].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What secure coding technique is employed specifically to defeat injection attacks (like SQL injection) by ensuring that user input is treated only as data, not as executable code?
Choices: Input validation
Output encoding
Escaping special characters
Parameterization (Prepared Statements)
Questions.AnswerKey: Parameterization (Prepared Statements)
Questions.Explaination: Parameterization, also known as using prepared statements, is the technique of using placeholders in the code for user input, ensuring the input is interpreted strictly as data rather than executable commands, making it a highly effective countermeasure against SQL injection [3]. Input validation (the close distractor) is a broader necessary step to check for acceptable data format, but parameterization is the specific mechanism that prevents the execution of input as code [3].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: During application processing, where is data categorized when it is actively stored in volatile memory, CPU registers, or caches, making it vulnerable to memory scraping attacks?
Choices: Data at rest
Data in motion
Data in transit
Data in use
Questions.AnswerKey: Data in use
Questions.Explaination: Data in use refers to data actively residing in memory (RAM) or processing areas (registers, caches), which is the most challenging state to protect because it must be in a decrypted or available format to the CPU [9]. Data in transit (the close distractor) refers to data moving across a network [9].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What application vulnerability allows an attacker to manipulate file paths, often using the '..\' or '../' sequences, to access resources or files outside the application’s intended root directory?
Choices: Improper error handling
Buffer overflow
Directory Traversal
Insecure direct object reference
Questions.AnswerKey: Directory Traversal
Questions.Explaination: Directory Traversal (or Path Traversal) attacks exploit poor input validation on file paths to allow attackers to access restricted directories or files, often using the double-dot sequence (..) [2]. Insecure direct object reference (the close distractor) allows access to objects (files, databases, etc.) that the user should not be able to reference, but usually without manipulating the directory structure itself.

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: Which access control model relies strictly on explicit classification labels assigned to subjects and objects, where the system makes all access decisions based on these defined security classifications, overriding discretionary policies?
Choices: Discretionary Access Control (DAC)
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC)
Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC)
Mandatory Access Control (MAC)
Questions.AnswerKey: Mandatory Access Control (MAC)
Questions.Explaination: Mandatory Access Control (MAC) uses explicit security classification labels (e.g., Secret, Top Secret) on all subjects and objects, and the system strictly enforces the access policy based on these mandatory labels, common in high-security governmental systems [22, 23]. Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), the best distractor, is based on functional roles within an organization but does not rely on strict sensitivity labels [24].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What secure design principle requires that if a system component fails (such as an authentication module), the system must default to a restrictive state, usually by denying access, to protect confidentiality and integrity?
Choices: Fail Open
Secure Defaults
Defense in Depth
Fail Securely
Questions.AnswerKey: Fail Securely
Questions.Explaination: The principle of Fail Securely mandates that when a component fails, the system defaults to the secure state (usually closed/deny access) to preserve assets [25, 26]. Secure Defaults (the close distractor) dictates the initial configuration state, whereas Fail Securely dictates the behavior during a failure event [26].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What code testing methodology involves submitting actual user inputs to a running application to observe how the program behaves during execution, often used to test performance and security flaws at runtime?
Choices: Static Program Analysis
Fuzzing
Dynamic Testing
Code Review
Questions.AnswerKey: Dynamic Testing
Questions.Explaination: Dynamic Testing involves executing the program with various inputs in a runtime environment to assess behavior, performance, and vulnerabilities [19, 21]. Static Program Analysis (the close distractor) analyzes the code without execution [21].

Questions.DomainOfKnowledge: CISSP Domain 8: Software Development Security
Questions.Question: What process is defined as categorizing organizational information and assets based on their value, sensitivity, and the potential impact to the business if they are disclosed, altered, or destroyed?
Choices: Data retention
Data encryption
Data classification
Data privacy
Questions.AnswerKey: Data classification
